c.tagline: Etruscan hill town and green heart of Italy, where medieval alleys, chocolate and jazz mingle with a lively student buzz.

taxi.fareNote: Licensed taxis are white and metered, with supplements for luggage, nights and holidays; Uber is essentially unavailable in Perugia (it operates only in a few large Italian cities), so use street/rank taxis or call a radio taxi.

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number and connects to all services; 113 reaches police and 118 reaches medical/ambulance directly.

avoid.reason: The Fontivegge station area feels seedy at night; keep an eye on bags during festival crowds.

hood_desc: The medieval hilltop heart of Perugia, centered on Corso Vannucci with Palazzo dei Priori, the Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria, Fontana Maggiore and Piazza IV Novembre — sights, cafes and evening strolls at every turn.
The old northern quarter around Porta Sant'Angelo and the Etruscan Arch, home to the Università per Stranieri, artisan workshops and a relaxed student-and-local mix just below the center.
A leafy residential district at the foot of the historic core beside the main university, full of students, everyday shops and quiet streets with easy access into town.
A calm hillside neighborhood just outside the medieval walls to the northeast, redeveloped around the old Monteluce hospital site with parks, apartments and local life.
The modern business-and-transport hub around Perugia's Fontivegge railway station and Minimetrò stop — gritty but supremely well connected for arriving, leaving and moving across the city.
lodging: Hotel Giò Wine e Jazz Area

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink.

transit.hours: ~6:00-21:15 (Minimetrò and city buses; limited night service)
transit.note: A single automated Minimetrò line links Pincetto (historic center) to Pian di Massiano via the Fontivegge railway station, with Busitalia city buses covering the rest. Escalators and elevators through the Rocca Paolina ease the climb up the steep hilltop.
transit.pay: Single ticket €1.50 (70 min) or €5.40 day pass; buy at Minimetrò machines and tabacchi. One ticket is valid on both the Minimetrò and city buses.

food.name: Torta al testo
food.desc: Umbria's flat griddle bread cooked on a hot stone disc, split and stuffed with sausage and greens, prosciutto, or cheese.

places.name: Testone
places.note: Dedicated torta al testo counter on Piazza Matteotti; classic salsiccia e erbe filling made to order.

places.name: Il Birraio
places.note: Casual central spot pairing hot torta al testo with local beer, popular with students.

places.name: Mercato Coperto
places.note: Covered market terrace with stalls griddling torta al testo beside city-wall views.

food.name: Strangozzi al tartufo
food.desc: Hand-rolled eggless Umbrian pasta, thick and chewy, tossed with black truffle, tomato or garlic-and-chilli sauce.

places.name: Ristorante Dal Cesarino
places.note: Serving Umbrian classics since 1973 beside the Fontana Maggiore; strangozzi al tartufo is the signature.

places.name: Osteria a Priori

places.name: Dal Mi Cocco

food.name: Porchetta
food.desc: Whole herb-and-fennel roasted pork, sliced with crackling and served in a crusty roll from market vans and delis.

places.name: Mercato Coperto

places.name: Sandwich Shop Perugia
places.note: Central takeaway stacking porchetta with local pecorino for a quick lunch.

places.name: Mercato di Pian di Massiano

places.name: Pasticceria Sandri

places.name: Perugina store Corso Vannucci

places.name: Antica Trattoria San Lorenzo
places.note: Refined Umbrian cooking by the cathedral; strong on game and local cured meats.

places.name: La Bottega di Perugia
places.note: Deli-osteria assembling boards of Norcia salumi and boar salami with Umbrian wine.

places.name: Osteria a Priori
places.note: Regional-only larder with excellent cinghiale salami and pecorino tastings.

food.name: Torciglione and rocciata

places.name: Il Bacio del Vino

places.name: Bottega del Vino

landmarks: Fontana Maggiore
A masterpiece of medieval sculpture by Nicola and Giovanni Pisano, this 13th-century pink-and-white fountain crowns Piazza IV Novembre with carved zodiac and biblical reliefs.
Palazzo dei Priori & Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria
The crenellated Gothic seat of city government houses Umbria's greatest art collection, from Piero della Francesca to hometown master Perugino.
Cattedrale di San Lorenzo
Perugia's unfinished Gothic cathedral on the main square, guarding the reputed wedding ring of the Virgin Mary behind fifteen locks.
Rocca Paolina
A buried papal fortress built over a razed medieval quarter, now an atmospheric underground city of vaulted streets threaded by public escalators.
Arco Etrusco (Etruscan Arch)
A colossal city gate built by the Etruscans in the third century BC, still bearing the inscriptions Augusta Perusia from its Roman refounding.
Collegio del Cambio
The Renaissance moneychangers' guild hall, frescoed floor-to-ceiling by Perugino, possibly assisted by his young pupil Raphael.
Pozzo Etrusco (Etruscan Well)
A staggering 37-meter engineering feat from the third century BC, descended today by dripping stone stairways beneath the old city.
Basilica di San Pietro
A tenth-century Benedictine basilica at the city's edge, its candlelit interior dense with canvases, intarsia choir stalls and a serene medieval garden.
Basilica di San Domenico
Umbria's largest church, holding the Gothic tomb of Pope Benedict XI and the region's archaeological museum in its tranquil cloisters.
Corso Vannucci
Perugia's marble-paved evening stage, a passeggiata boulevard running between palazzi, chocolate shops and cafés to the panoramic Giardini Carducci terrace.

train.note: No international trains. Perugia Fontivegge station is down in the valley, linked to the hilltop centre by the MiniMetrò automated shuttle. Regional trains reach Assisi in 25 minutes, Florence in about two hours and Rome in 2h30; there is no high-speed line, so long journeys often involve a change at Foligno or Terontola. Regional fares are fixed-price.

bus.note: Coaches use Piazza Partigiani below the old town, connected by escalators through the Rocca Paolina. Busitalia (https://www.fsbusitalia.it/) runs the Umbrian network to Assisi, Gubbio and Lake Trasimeno, and Sulga runs direct coaches to Rome Tiburtina and Fiumicino airport in about 2h30, which is usually faster than the train.

ferry.note: Perugia is inland in Umbria with no port. Passenger boats do run on nearby Lake Trasimeno, about 30 minutes west, linking Passignano and Tuoro with Isola Maggiore, but these are lake services rather than transport to or from the city.

half.name: Assisi
half.blurb: St. Francis's hometown, with its frescoed basilica on a hillside, is about thirty minutes from Perugia.

half.name: Gubbio
half.blurb: A medieval stone town with a funicular to a hilltop basilica lies roughly forty-five minutes from Perugia.

half.name: Lake Trasimeno
half.blurb: Umbria's largest lake has island ferries and lakeside towns about thirty minutes from Perugia.

half.name: Spoleto
half.blurb: A Roman-era hill town with a soaring medieval aqueduct bridge sits roughly an hour from Perugia.

half.name: Todi
half.blurb: A hilltop town with a Renaissance temple and a panoramic piazza lies about forty-five minutes from Perugia.
